newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ANALYSTS SAY WAIT, THEN BUY CZECH CKD.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS SAY WAIT, THEN BUY CZECH CKD.

text.p: Shares in Czech engineering firm CKD Praha a.s. which have risen sharply since the beginning of the year, are a long-term buy despite a possible short-term corretion in the issue, analysts said.
CKD continued the soar on the Prague Stock Exchange on Wednesday, rising 45 crowns to 963 at the bourse's daily price fixing, a rise of some 66 percent over the first two months of 1997.

While recommending the shares over the long-term, analysts surveyed by Reuters said they saw a better buying opportunity after an expected price correction, though estimates varied on the buy level at between 600 and 800 crowns.
"I don't think (the shares) would be overvalued now. I have been expecting the rise for a long time," said Petr Hajek of Zivnostenska Banka.

Added Akro Capital's Tomas Navratil: "The company is able to win important orders, and has shown it can penetrate new markets, especially in the East. It also has the possibility to service and repair orders in the future."
CKD Praha focuses on the production of trains and other rail vehicles, including underground carriages and trams.

Orders last year from the Philippines for trams, a deal to supply the Prague underground with subway cars, and one to build trains for a future high-speed railway corridor connecting Vienna and Berlin via Prague have also boosted CKD in the eyes of investors.
CKD shares recorded a similar jump in mid-1996, when they rose 240 crowns 400 in a matter of weeks. "The interest for CKD shares comes mainly from foreign investors," said Navratil.
Analysts said the company still lacks blue chip status on the market because it has yet to finish organisational and financial restructuring plans.

"(The firm's) financial healing is far from finished, and the company will, above all, have to solve a problem of indebtedness...since bank loans exceed its basic capital," Leos Jirman of Delta Securities told Reuters.
Analysts expect the firm to post a 1.7 billion crown loss in 1996, but see CKD returning to profitability this year. The firm has yet to provide full 1996 results.
"(CKD's holding company) should end the year with a consolidated net profit of over 300 million crowns," Hajek said.
